verses.verse:
यत्र रागस्य मुख्यांगम् तालस्यादौ विधीयते।
गुरूवर्णस्य तत्रैव संगमः सम उच्यते।१३५।
verses.text: Where the main part of the rāga is placed at the start of the tāla, and a long syllable meets it right there, that meeting is called sam.

commentary.text: That is, where on the first mātrā the main part of the rāga and some long syllable of the words come together and, as if from colliding with each other, seem to halt - this confluence of three streams is called sam (first beat of the cycle). For example, in the song "madhuvan meṃ rādhikā nācī re" [Rādhikā danced in Madhuvan], the main part of the words (nā), the main part of the rāga (Dha) and the first mātrā of the tāla - these three meet and it becomes full of rasa. This is the special quality of sam.

following.text: Method of composing a gat (gat nirmāṇa)
Now, having understood the importance of sam, nyāsa, tāla and words, we must move on to composing a gat or gīt. On this subject the following methods are described.
